assertion_analysis.failure_condition: test_quiet_cycles_list_nothing_and_spawn_no_git counts real calls: _install_list_counter wraps recovery_watch.list_live and _install_spawn_counter counts git argv seen by subprocess.run. Reinstating the fixed-beat sweep advances the listing counter at every boundary, so `marks['list'][1] == marks['list'][0]    ` and `marks['spawn'][1] == marks['spawn'][0]` redden. Neither side is a value the test handed to the code; the counters observe the code's own calls, so the assertion is independent of the value under test.

test_a_touched_pointer_sweeps_exactly_once asserts `marks[1] - marks[0] == 1`, marks being list_live call counts read at boundaries while os.utime moves a pointer's mtime. This is the assertion the declared negative control reddens (negative-control.log, `assert (1 - 1) == 1`), so its failure condition is demonstrated: a token whose per-run entry ignores the pointer leaves the touch invisible and the delta 0.

test_a_death_is_delivered_within_one_beat_with_no_file_change flips the fixture's monkeypatched liveness flag (tests/test_a_producer_sweeps_only_on_change.py:111-117) and asserts the yielded transitions name every live run. If _quiet_beat_snapshots dropped its _fresh_liveness re-probe and served the cached snapshot, no transition would be yielded and the assertion would redden. The liveness source is the fixture's own flag, not a value the assertion passes to the code.

Each of these five cases writes one gated input (budget_lift.lifts_path(), an EXIT_RECORD_NAME in the run directory, a handover record, a review-store candidate, a commit in the run's worktree) on a quiet beat and asserts `marks[1] - marks[0] == 1` then `marks[2] == marks[1]`. Dropping that input from the token leaves the write invisible and the delta 0. All five are demonstrated reddened: negative-control.log pins the per-run token entry to a constant and fails four of them (the lift and handover cases reach the token through directory stamps and carry their own coverage-mutations.log controls, EXIT=1 each). The counter observes list_live, not the input the test wrote, so the assertions are independent of the value under test.

test_the_change_token_stamps_the_crew_home_through_the_shared_reader asserts each of runs.live_dir(), runs.runs_dir(), runs.handover_dir() and budget_lift.lifts_path() appears in the paths passed to capabilities.file_stamp. This is a shape assertion: it reddens if the token stops stamping a directory (or stops using the shared reader) but it would pass even if a stamped directory failed to move the gate, so it complements, rather than substitutes for, the behavioural cases above. The path strings compared are the token's own calls, not a value the test supplied to the code.

findings.text: follow-on: _quiet_beat_snapshots (recovery_watch.py:2275) re-implements the stored-snapshot liveness-resume decision that _watch_snapshot (recovery_watch.py:1272) already owns. The block `_fresh_liveness(pointer) != (stored.get('process_alive'), stored.get('liveness_proven'), stored.get('process_descendant_alive'))` followed by `_refresh_snapshot(stored, ...)` stands at recovery_watch.py:1300-1307 and again at recovery_watch.py:2305-2316. The two differ only in that the quiet path skips the _snapshot_reuse_key fan-out, which is exactly why it cannot simply call _watch_snapshot -- but the liveness tuple is one fact with two copies, and the recompute fallback is delegated to the owner rather than duplicated. A change to the tuple's composition must now be made in both. The worker names this as a follow_on in its manifest; recorded, not held.

follow-on: _stop_delivered_reviews is moved from the every-beat body (base recovery_watch.py:2414) into the WATCHER_SWEEP_INTERVAL_SECONDS (30 s) cadence block at recovery_watch.py:2526-2535, so a delivered review whose stream has outlived its 300 s grace (recovery_review_delivery.py:41) is stopped up to 30 s later than before. The move is consistent with the goal ('only the per-run liveness probe on the fixed beat') and the added latency is ~10 % of the grace, so it is benign; it is recorded because it is a behaviour change the goal and done_when do not name, and the manifest describes the two clock sweeps as riding 'their own cadence on every beat' where sweep_unfollowed_sessions and the review stop both ride the 30 s cadence. Not held.

follow-on: the landing fragment's negative-control paragraph says the constant-pin mutation 'fails exactly the two cases that assert a gated input moves the gate: the pointer whose mtime is touched, and the exit record written on a quiet beat.' At the reviewed head the same control fails four cases (negative-control.log: test_a_touched_pointer_sweeps_exactly_once, test_a_run_record_written_on_a_quiet_beat_sweeps, test_a_review_record_written_on_a_quiet_beat_sweeps, test_a_worktree_head_moved_on_a_quiet_beat_sweeps), because c433cf0de added the last two cases without updating this sentence. The authoritative log is correct; the fragment understates the coverage it reports. Documentation accuracy only, does not hold the node.

item_verdicts.diff: Read commit by commit against 284c31716. 2f129ebc9 gates the watch_ticker loop on a stat-only home token and adds _stat_stamp, _crew_home_change_token, _run_streams and _quiet_beat_snapshots plus the new test file; d84d1d601 adds the landing fragment; a6e4fca22 rewrites the fragment's measurement to fleet scale; 11a271be1 widens the token to the whole per-run composition (_snapshot_reuse_key), adds the lift document and handover directory, drops _stat_stamp for capabilities.file_stamp, and takes the orphan sweep and review-stop off the gate onto the 30 s cadence; af75c342b edits the fragment to record the coverage and cost; c433cf0de adds the three per-input cases (handover, review store candidate, worktree head) and removes the stray closing tag. Three files total, all inside the declared scope.
item_verdicts.done_when: The node done_when has three arms. Arms one and two (quiet cycles take no directory walk and no git-shim spawn, then a touched pointer pulls exactly one sweep) are asserted by tests/test_a_producer_sweeps_only_on_change.py:182-205 and :208-226; arm three (a death with no file moved still transitions within one beat) by tests/test_a_producer_sweeps_only_on_change.py:229-242. Arm two's separate strace requirement is recorded in fleet-syscall-gate.log: per quiet cycle the change costs 79.7/30.0 openat and 85.3/44.0 stat against the base's 1211.3 openat and 868.3 stat -- 6.6 % on openat and 9.8 % on stat, below the done_when's literal tenth of 1880 and 1575, with 0.0 git spawns against the base's 1.9. The measured base (1211/868) does not reproduce the done_when's 1880/1575 literally; it is the same order and the ratio targets hold either way.
item_verdicts.goal: The node goal is to make the crew watch producer run its live listing, run-directory walk and git sweeps only when the crew home changes, keeping only the per-run liveness probe on the fixed beat. Landed: recovery_watch.py:2503 computes _crew_home_change_token (recovery_watch.py:2218) each poll and recovery_watch.py:2505-2515 takes the handover read, the listing, the token refresh and the lift fold only under `if sweep:`; recovery_watch.py:2537-2554 takes _watch_snapshot on a sweeping beat and _quiet_beat_snapshots (recovery_watch.py:2275) on a quiet one, and the quiet path re-takes only _fresh_liveness per run. The watch directory is deliberately excluded from the token (its seat record is rewritten every poll), which is what makes the saving real.
